title: Operations Assistant: Repair a Front-Desk Schedule
prompt: Fictional Rowan Community Centre needs reception coverage from 09:00 to 17:00. Busy periods require two trained people from 09:00 to 10:00 and 12:00 to 13:00; other times require one. Draft: Alex 09:00–13:00, Bea 12:00–17:00. Bea must leave from 14:00 to 14:30 for an appointment. You are a coordinator, not their manager. Review the gaps and propose a plan to confirm. Do not assume staff can work outside their agreed availability.
blurb: Find coverage gaps, work within staff availability, and prepare a rota ready for manager confirmation.

rubric.label: Identify coverage gaps
rubric.description: Checks the schedule against intervals and required staffing.

anchors.0: Says overlapping shifts cover the entire day or misses the 14:00 absence.
anchors.2: Finds the missing second person at 09:00 and no cover at 14:00.
anchors.4: Checks all stated intervals, preserves the valid noon overlap, and distinguishes known gaps from unresolved break coverage.

rubric.label: Use real availability
rubric.description: Proposes changes consistent with supplied availability and authority.

anchors.0: Extends Alex’s shift or commits Chris without checking availability and approval.
anchors.2: Requests available trained backup for the uncovered intervals.
anchors.4: Uses Chris as a proposed solution to both gaps, seeks approval, and makes break information a condition of publishing the final plan.

rubric.label: Make the schedule dependable
rubric.description: Communicates confirmed staffing and contingency ownership.

anchors.0: Publishes a proposed rota as confirmed or leaves the desk unattended without a plan.
anchors.2: Confirms changes with staff and the manager.
anchors.4: Labels proposed versus confirmed shifts, records a contact for absence escalation, and asks the manager for a contingency if cover is declined.

reference.scenario: Fictional Rowan Community Centre needs reception coverage from 09:00 to 17:00. Busy periods require two trained people from 09:00 to 10:00 and 12:00 to 13:00; other times require one. Draft: Alex 09:00–13:00, Bea 12:00–17:00. Bea must leave from 14:00 to 14:30 for an appointment. You are a coordinator, not their manager. Review the gaps and propose a plan to confirm. Do not assume staff can work outside their agreed availability.

facts.value: Chris is trained and available 09:00–10:00 and 14:00–15:00, subject to manager approval. Alex cannot stay after 13:00.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about approved backup coverage or staff availability

facts.value: Fictional centre policy requires the manager to confirm break coverage and approve schedule changes. Staff break needs have not yet been collected.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about breaks, scheduling policy, or approval

model_points: The draft meets the two-person noon requirement but not the 09:00–10:00 requirement. Bea’s 14:00–14:30 absence leaves nobody after Alex ends at 13:00.
Chris’s stated availability could fill both known gaps, but approval is required. There is no basis for extending Alex or assuming untrained staff can cover reception.
Ask about break needs before calling the full rota complete. Show the manager the proposed changes and unresolved items in a simple coverage table; do not invent statutory break rules.

probes.trigger: candidate proposes only covering Bea’s appointment
probes.question: How many people are at reception from 09:00 to 10:00?
Which approvals and break details are still missing?

fair_alternatives: A manager arranging another trained worker is valid if Chris is unavailable or approval is declined.
A table or a spoken interval-by-interval check is equally acceptable.
red_flags: Says overlapping shifts cover the entire day or misses the 14:00 absence.
Extends Alex’s shift or commits Chris without checking availability and approval.
Publishes a proposed rota as confirmed or leaves the desk unattended without a plan.
follow_ups: Create a six-row coverage check showing time, required people, planned people, gap, and proposed owner.
reference.exemplar_answer: The noon overlap is sufficient, but the opening hour needs a second person and the desk is uncovered during Bea’s appointment. I would propose Chris for those intervals and ask the manager to approve the change. Before publishing it, I would collect break needs and confirm their cover. The schedule would distinguish proposed and confirmed names and say who to contact if a replacement is unavailable.

interviewer_notes: Assess basic coordination and careful checking. The break rule is specific to the fictional centre; no employment-law knowledge is required. Do not infer that approved backup is guaranteed. Use only supplied facts; say when something is unknown. Accept plain language and equivalent approaches. Assess the demonstrated decisions, not accent, confidence, credentials, or access to particular employers. This is a fictional exercise; do not imply real actions were performed.

learning_drills.title: Check a rota by interval
learning_drills.prompt: Create a six-row coverage check showing time, required people, planned people, gap, and proposed owner. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Mark approval and break details as pending
